title: The friendship paradox: Causal evidence of its behavioral consequences
abstract: arXiv:2608.07819v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We provide a first causal analysis of the behavioral consequences of the friendship paradox-the fact that people's friends in a network have more connections than average. We find that people's behavior is biased by their network position: they do not best respond to what they should infer the average behavior of the population to be (which determines their payoff), but instead best respond to the average behavior of their friends. In these games of complements, the friendship paradox generates a systematic upward distortion in actions and increases behavioral dispersion. These behavioral distortions persist despite learning opportunities: subjects fail to overcome the bias even when relocated within the network which should help them to understand how average population behavior can differ from local friend behavior.

translated_title: 友谊悖论：其行为后果的因果证据
translated_abstract: 我们首次对友谊悖论——即网络中人们的朋友平均而言比本人拥有更多连接这一事实——的行为后果进行了因果分析。我们发现人们的行为会受到其网络位置的偏误影响：他们并非针对其应推断出的总体平均行为（这决定了他们的收益）做出最优反应，而是针对其朋友的平均行为做出最优反应。在这类互补性博弈中，友谊悖论导致了行为的系统性向上扭曲，并加大了行为离散度。这些行为扭曲在学习机会存在的情况下依然持续存在：即使当受试者被在网络中重新安置——这本应帮助他们理解总体平均行为如何区别于朋友平均行为——他们仍然无法克服这种偏误。
tldr: 该研究首次通过因果分析证明，友谊悖论会使个体基于朋友的平均行为而非总体平均行为做出决策，导致行为出现系统性向上偏高的扭曲，且即使提供学习机会也难以纠正这种偏误。
